summary:
The research points to one foundation: a deterministic, data-driven simulation engine in pure Swift, kept apart from a thin native iOS shell and guarded by strict CI gates. Each known failure mode gets a structural fix, so the fix does not depend on discipline.

(1) No WebView and no JavaScript. In Swift, a duplicate declaration in the same scope is a compile error ('invalid redeclaration'), and missing enum cases are compile errors too. The old failure mode, a later 'patch' function silently overriding an earlier one, therefore cannot compile.
(2) Real source trees only. Commit no zips. CI rejects archives and generates the Xcode project from XcodeGen's project.yml. XcodeGen's ProjectSpec confirms that a Target has no `resources` key: resources come only from `sources`, using `buildPhase: resources` or `type: folder`.
(3) An IPA gate checks the bundle against a content manifest and SHA-256 hashes, plus size limits and Info.plist keys.
(4) Content is read directly from the read-only app bundle. It is never copied to Application Support.

Modules (one SwiftPM package at the repo root, Swift 6 language mode), with dependencies flowing one way only:
- Core: typed IDs, Int64 money, calendar, deterministic RNG and math, state hash, ring buffers.
- Content: strict loaders, validator, immutable ContentDB, memory-mapped map.bin reader.
- Engine: SoA (structure-of-arrays) world state, commands, ordered systems pipeline, invariants, save codec and migrations.
- AI and Presentation: map-mode colour functions, Arabic formatters, 'explain' breakdowns.
- simcli: a headless validate/run/replay/bench/balance tool.
- iOS side: an App target (SwiftUI) and a MapRenderer target (Metal), generated by XcodeGen, plus Python map tools.

Everything except App and MapRenderer builds and tests on Linux. Swift Testing is supported on Linux and ships in the Swift 6 toolchain. Free ubuntu-24.04-arm runners also let CI compare state hashes across x86_64 and arm64.

Data model:
- Data files use stable, namespaced lowercase string IDs. These are interned at load into dense Int32 indices, sorted by ID so the order is deterministic.
- Static content (immutable class) is kept separate from dynamic state (value-type struct of column arrays). Swift's copy-on-write makes an O(1) snapshot for the UI thread and for autosave.
- Saves never store dense indices. They store per-kind ID lists, so content can add provinces, countries or entity kinds without breaking old saves.
- Dynamic entities (armies, fleets, projects, treaties, later trade routes and companies) live in tables with generational handles.
- New features add a table, a system, command cases and a save section. They do not migrate the base.

Content:
- Content packs (JSON) have a pack.json manifest with formatVersion. The base game is itself a pack.
- The same Swift loader that runs in the app runs in CI. It rejects unknown keys (JSONDecoder ignores them by default, so the loader compares keys explicitly), resolves every reference, checks ranges, coverage and adjacency symmetry, and checks that Arabic localisation keys exist.
- An ID that already exists can be changed only through an explicit `override` block. A plain duplicate is an error, which avoids the silent last-wins override seen in Paradox mod load order.
- All tuning numbers live in defines.json, and all bonuses go through one typed modifier catalog. Tech, laws, events, difficulty, presets and cheats all apply modifiers.

Simulation:
- A daily tick runs fixed-order stages declared in one Pipeline file, with cadences of daily, monthly and yearly. Heavy AI work is staggered across days. Victoria 3 Dev Diary #76 describes the same split into yearly/monthly/weekly/daily/'tickly' tasks, with a parallel pre-step and sorting to avoid multiplayer desyncs.
- Every mutation by player or AI is a Codable Command that is validated and then applied at the tick boundary. This is Nystrom's 'reified method call' pattern, which gives AI parity, replays and serialisation.
- Notifications sit in a bounded ring buffer. Treasury changes only through a ledger, so money conservation can be checked.
- Determinism rules:
  - Use a counter-based seeded RNG and our own range mapping. SE-0202's SystemRandomNumberGenerator cannot be seeded, and the stdlib does not promise its algorithms stay stable.
  - Never iterate a Dictionary or Set in the Engine, because Swift seeds hashing randomly per process.
  - No libm transcendental functions (sin, exp, log, pow). They differ between platforms, which is why Factorio uses its own implementations after a sin() desync between Windows and Linux. Use Core.DMath instead.
  - Use Int64 for stocks (money, people, manpower).
  - Hash the state every day in replay mode. This is Factorio's per-tick CRC technique.

Performance evidence:
- I measured Natural Earth 10m admin-1 (public domain): 4,596 units, 8,535 polygon parts, 1,286,673 vertices, 251 ADM0 codes, and name_ar filled for 4,589 of 4,596. Some countries are over-split (GBR 232, SVN 193), so the pipeline must merge units into game provinces and edit them to the 1985 borders. It also needs sea zones from day one.
- A C benchmark of the SoA layout (6,000 provinces × 32 columns, 200 countries) averaged 141 µs per simulated day, with 1.5 MB of state. Province arithmetic is cheap. The real cost will be the AI, pathfinding and rendering.

Lightness:
- Map meshes are triangulated offline with LODs and memory-mapped at load. Map modes only change a per-province colour buffer. Each border segment stores its two provinces, so country borders follow ownership on the GPU.
- MTKView runs event-driven: paused, with enableSetNeedsDisplay set.
- The HUD uses @Observable, which re-renders only the properties a view reads, throttled to about 4 Hz.
- Frame rate and maximum speed are capped when the device's thermal state or Low Power Mode calls for it.

Saves:
- A header plus metadata JSON, then a columnar payload with ID lists, compressed, with a checksum.
- An integer formatVersion with a migration chain on the untyped JSON tree, plus content alias tables for renamed or split IDs.
- Golden saves are never deleted and are loaded on every CI run.
- Atomic, rotating autosaves.

Localization: Arabic first. UI strings go in a String Catalog and content strings in pack loc files, both keyed. The engine never produces display text. The map stays left-to-right inside a mirrored UI. Plurals use the six CLDR Arabic categories. Digits are a user setting (Arabic-Indic or Western), applied through the `@numbers=` locale subtag. In iOS 18 Apple changed the plain `ar` default to Western digits, except in Arabic-speaking regions.

Publishing and licensing: since April 28, 2026, App Store uploads need Xcode 26 and the iOS 26 SDK. The deployment target can stay at iOS 17, so CI should use the macos-26 runner. A SOURCES.json license registry, checked by CI, allows only PD, CC0, CC BY, OFL or MIT data and assets. GADM is excluded because it is non-commercial. CShapes 2.0 is non-commercial and may be used only as a human cross-check. geoBoundaries needs a per-release license check.

Process: CLAUDE.md conventions, immutable ADRs (superseded by new ones, never edited), a definition of done, file-size and duplication gates (SwiftLint, and jscpd with --fail-on-new-clones 0), and branch protection so that only a green PR reaches main. The user reviews and merges from the phone and downloads the IPA artifact.

Web-research limits: Paradox, Factorio and some Apple pages could not be fetched (DNS), so claims about them rely on search snippets. The shared web-search budget then ran out mid-research, so a few references (Fabian's DOD book, Acton's talk, Paradox defines files, iOS 17 device floor) appear under 'unverified'.

items.finding: XcodeGen Targets have no 'resources' key. Resources come only through 'sources', using 'buildPhase: resources' or 'type: folder' (a folder reference). A target-level 'resources' key is ignored, so an app can build green yet ship with no game files. Fix: put Content in as a folder reference under sources, and add a CI IPA gate that checks every file in the manifest.
items.evidence: https://github.com/yonaskolb/XcodeGen/blob/master/Docs/ProjectSpec.md (fetched: target sources accept buildPhase 'resources'; 'type: folder' gives a folder reference; no resources key listed)

items.topic: Old failure: duplicated or overriding functions
items.finding: Moving from one JS file to Swift modules removes silent overrides structurally. Swift rejects an 'invalid redeclaration' in the same scope, and exhaustive enum switches force every handler to update when a Command case is added. Add file-length limits (SwiftLint file_length and type_body_length, which run on Linux) and copy-paste detection (jscpd with --fail-on-new-clones 0 against a main baseline; Swift is covered in its similarity mode).
items.evidence: https://github.com/realm/SwiftLint (Linux supported; file_length and type_body_length rules); https://github.com/kucherenko/jscpd (224 formats, Swift similarity, '--baseline-from-ref origin/main --fail-on-new-clones 0'); the Swift redeclaration error is compiler behaviour (reasoning)

items.finding: Paradox added Jomini as a shared layer between game-specific code and the Clausewitz engine (Imperator, 2019). The goal was to move duplicated code out of individual games so features could be reused. Lesson: put reusable simulation infrastructure (IDs, tables, RNG, commands, saves, content loading) in Core, Content and Engine, and keep game rules in systems and data.
items.evidence: WebSearch summary of forum.paradoxplaza.com Jomini modding manuscript, pcgamesn.com/imperator-rome/paradox-new-engine-jomini, dsogaming (Paradox pages themselves could not be fetched: DNS)

items.finding: Victoria 3 Dev Diary #76 (2023-02-23): a tick is 6 in-game hours, and tasks are split into yearly, monthly, weekly, daily and per-tick categories. The most expensive tasks run weekly. A parallel pre-step on task threads is followed by a serial main-thread step, with a sorting step to prevent multiplayer desyncs. Pop counts grow from about 20–25k at start to about 100k. Dev Diary #142: update 1.6 was slower for most users because AI and migration changes cost more than the optimisations saved. They built an internal Performance Dashboard heatmap. Lesson: declare a cadence per system, stagger per-country AI, and add a performance regression gate before features grow.
items.evidence: WebSearch results quoting forum.paradoxplaza.com/forum/developer-diary/victoria-3-dev-diary-76-performance.1570277 and ...-dev-diary-142-2024-in-retrospect.1726056 (snippets only; full pages unreachable)

items.finding: Mathieu Ropert's ACCU 2023 talk covers three threading models: the 'old' one (EU4, HOI4, Stellaris; Intel TBB), the one introduced with CK3, and future directions. Recommendation: start single-threaded but declare reads and writes per system, so a later parallel pre-step with a deterministic reduce is an addition, not a rewrite.
items.evidence: WebSearch: accu.org/video/spring-2023-day-3/ropert and the ACCU 2023 slides PDF abstract (talk details not fetched)

items.finding: Nystrom defines a command as 'a reified method call'. Keeping the last command enables undo. The AI can use 'this same command pattern as the interface between the AI engine and the actors'. Serialisable commands can be sent over the network or replayed. Recommendation: one Codable `enum Command`, validate(state) then apply(&state), used identically by player UI, AI, replays and bug reports.
items.evidence: https://github.com/munificent/game-programming-patterns/blob/master/book/command.markdown (fetched)

items.finding: Swift's Dictionary and Set use randomly seeded hashing, so iteration order changes between runs. SWIFT_DETERMINISTIC_HASHING=1 fixes the seed for testing only, and hash values are not stable across stdlib versions. Rule: never iterate a Dictionary or Set in Engine or AI. Use index-ordered arrays or a sorted or ordered collection.
items.evidence: https://forums.swift.org/t/psa-the-stdlib-now-uses-randomly-seeded-hash-values/10789 ; Apple DTS answer in developer.apple.com/forums/thread/770525 (via search)

items.finding: SE-0202's SystemRandomNumberGenerator has only init(), with no seed. Custom generators implement `mutating func next() -> UInt64`. The proposal does not promise that random(in:using:) or shuffle produce stable sequences across Swift versions. Rule: Core.DetRNG uses SplitMix64 or a counter-based hash keyed by (gameSeed, day, systemStream, entityIndex), and our own documented range mapping. Golden-value tests lock the sequences.
items.evidence: https://github.com/swiftlang/swift-evolution/blob/main/proposals/0202-random-unification.md (fetched)

items.finding: Basic IEEE-754 operations (+ − × ÷ sqrt) are reproducible. sin, exp, log and pow come from the platform libm and differ in the last ulp between glibc, Apple and others. Fiedler says floating point can be made deterministic with one compiler and one instruction set. A Factorio developer traced a Windows/Linux desync to math.sin, and the engine uses its own implementations of most math functions. Rules: stocks (money, population, manpower, equipment) are Int64; rates may be Double with basic operations only; any curve uses Core.DMath (polynomial or table approximations built from basic ops); CI compares x86_64 and arm64 state hashes.
items.evidence: https://gafferongames.com/post/floating_point_determinism/ ; https://rapier.rs/docs/user_guides/templates/determinism/ ; https://arxiv.org/pdf/cs/0701192 ; https://forums.factorio.com/viewtopic.php?p=380365 (all via search snippets)

items.finding: Factorio computes a CRC of the whole map every tick and checks it during replays. On a mismatch, developers compare human-readable saves from the same tick to find the single diverging variable (FFF #47). A lighter per-tick heuristic CRC was used during multiplayer testing (FFF #55). Recommendation: StateHasher over all columns. simcli replay compares hashes each day and dumps a column-level diff at the first mismatch.
items.evidence: https://direct.factorio.com/blog/post/fff-47 and https://factorio.com/blog/post/fff-55 (via search snippets)

items.finding: Measured a struct-of-arrays daily tick in C (-O2) on an x86 Linux machine: 6,000 provinces × 32 Float64 columns updated daily, aggregation into 200 countries, and a monthly 200×200 relation pass. Average 141 µs per day, 0.52 s for 3,650 days, about 1.5 MB of province state. Province-level arithmetic is negligible, so the budget risk is AI, pathfinding, UI invalidation and rendering. Stagger the AI and gate tick time in CI.
items.evidence: Local benchmark wf/fnd/soa.c (output: avg_day=141.1us, worst_day=5336.9us including OS noise, state 1.54 MB)

items.finding: Natural Earth 10m admin-1 GeoJSON (local copy, version not determined) has 4,596 features, 8,535 polygon parts, 1,286,673 vertices and 251 ADM0 codes. name_ar is present for 4,589 of 4,596. ne_id and adm1_code are available for stable mapping. Some countries are far too granular (GBR 232 units, SVN 193, LVA 119), so the pipeline must merge units into game provinces. Full-resolution vertices take about 10 MB as Float32 pairs, so ship simplified LODs. About 1 s to parse the 40 MB GeoJSON in Python means it must be preprocessed offline, never parsed on the phone.
items.evidence: Measured with wf/fnd/count.py and props.py on wf/ne/ne10_admin1.geojson

items.finding: Natural Earth calls itself 'a public domain map dataset ... free for use in any type of project'. Natural Earth's forum notes that a few admin-1 attribute columns depend on GADM and advises non-US users to check locally. GADM is for academic and non-commercial use only, with no redistribution or commercial use without permission, so it is excluded. CShapes 2.0 (historical borders 1886–2019) is listed as CC BY-NC 4.0 or CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, non-commercial either way, so it can be a human cross-check reference only. geoBoundaries describes its data as CC BY 4.0 / ODbL, and the license must be checked per release.
items.evidence: https://github.com/nvkelso/natural-earth-vector ; https://www.naturalearthdata.com/?p=3348 ; https://lists.openstreetmap.org/pipermail/legal-talk/2015-August/008178.html ; https://www.research-collection.ethz.ch/handle/20.500.11850/487987 ; https://geo.btaa.org/catalog/b23a624e-f1ab-4989-8c94-f99f6e6fa414 ; https://github.com/wmgeolab/geoBoundaries

items.finding: Apple confirmed that in iOS 18 the default numbering system for plain `ar` changed to Western digits. Regions where Arabic is widely spoken (e.g. ar_SA) still default to Arabic-Indic digits. Users can change this in Language & Region, which shows up as a subtag such as `ar_US@numbers=arab`. Recommendation: an in-game setting with three choices (system, Arabic-Indic, Western) applied through a `@numbers=` subtag in one GameFormatter. Never hand-convert digits.
items.evidence: https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/773692 (fetched, Apple engineer answer); CLDR numbering systems https://cldr.unicode.org/translation/core-data/numbering-systems

items.finding: CLDR plural categories for Arabic are zero, one, two, few (n%100 in 3..10), many (n%100 in 11..99) and other. The String Catalog for UI strings and the content loc format must both support all six variants.
items.evidence: MDN Intl.PluralRules reference and Koha Arabic plural formula (via search)

items.finding: The Observation framework (SE-0395, @Observable, iOS 17+, which matches the minimum OS) tracks only the properties a view actually reads, so 'updates are only performed in response to relevant changes'. Recommendation: HUD and panel view models are @Observable and updated from engine snapshots at most about 4 Hz. Do not put per-tick values in SwiftUI environment objects.
items.evidence: https://github.com/swiftlang/swift-evolution/blob/main/proposals/0395-observability.md (fetched)

items.finding: MTKView supports event-driven drawing when isPaused and enableSetNeedsDisplay are both true, so the view redraws only after setNeedsDisplay. Apple recommends this for apps whose updates follow data changes. Apple does not quantify the battery saving, so it should be verified with Instruments.
items.evidence: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metalkit/mtkview/enablesetneedsdisplay (via search)

items.finding: GitHub-hosted images include macos-26 arm64 (labels macos-latest, macos-26), macos-15 arm64, macOS 14 (deprecated) and an Xcode 27 preview. Linux arm64 images are ubuntu-24.04-arm and ubuntu-26.04-arm. Standard runners are free and unlimited for public repositories. On paid plans the per-minute list prices are about $0.062 for macOS versus $0.002 for Linux, so run most gates on Linux and the macOS job only for the IPA and simulator smoke test.
items.evidence: https://github.com/actions/runner-images (fetched); https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/runners/github-hosted-runners ; https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-server@3.14/billing/reference/actions-runner-pricing (via search)

items.finding: Since April 28, 2026, uploads to App Store Connect must be built with Xcode 26 or later and the iOS 26 SDK. The deployment target can stay at iOS 17. The CI macOS job should pin Xcode 26.x on macos-26 now, so the project never needs reworking before publishing.
items.evidence: https://developer.apple.com/news/upcoming-requirements/ (via search) ; https://expo.dev/blog/app-store-connect-minimum-sdk-26

items.finding: Swift Testing is supported on Linux (automated CI) and ships with the Swift 6 toolchain and Xcode 16, with no package dependency needed. So Core, Content, Engine, AI and Presentation, plus every invariant, golden-save, replay and balance test, can run on cheap Linux runners on every push.
items.evidence: https://github.com/swiftlang/swift-testing (fetched)

items.finding: An ADR records one architecture decision with its context and consequences. Do not change existing information. Amend it, or supersede it with a new ADR. Fits the 'never go back and rebuild' condition: every foundation choice gets an ADR, and the AI assistant reads them before changing anything.
items.evidence: https://github.com/joelparkerhenderson/architecture-decision-record (fetched)

items.finding: In Paradox games, which mod file wins depends on lexical order of mod folder names, replace_path and dependencies, and load order matters only when files collide. This implicit override behaviour confuses modders and is the data-level version of a 'later patch wins' bug. Recommendation: duplicate IDs are a validation error unless a later pack declares an explicit override, and the active pack list plus content hash are shown and saved.
items.evidence: WebSearch results from admin-forum.paradoxplaza.com modding quick-questions threads (snippets); the CK3 wiki could not be fetched (DNS)

items.topic: Single source for display and simulation numbers
items.finding: Each derived value (stability, income, research speed) is computed by one pure function that returns a list of terms (source, contribution). The system sums the terms, and the UI tooltip shows the same list for the selected country only. Tooltip and simulation can therefore never disagree, and balancing is explainable. This is a design recommendation, not taken from a source.
items.evidence: Design reasoning (Paradox-style breakdown tooltips; no source fetched)

recommendations:
1) Repository layout, one source of truth per fact. Root `Package.swift` (swift-tools-version 6.0, Swift 6 language mode, platforms iOS 17 / macOS 14; Linux implicit). Folders:
- `Sources/{SaneiCore,SaneiContent,SaneiEngine,SaneiAI,SaneiPresentation,simcli}` and matching `Tests/*`, plus `Tests/Golden/{saves,replays}`.
- `App/project.yml` (XcodeGen; the .xcodeproj is generated in CI and gitignored), `App/Sources/{App,MapRenderer,Platform}`, and `App/Resources/{Assets.xcassets,Localizable.xcstrings}`.
- `content/packs/{base,scenario_1985}` (hand-edited JSON).
- `content/map/world-v1/` (GENERATED; a header and manifest name the generator and source hashes).
- `content/SOURCES.json` (license registry).
- `tools/map/` (Python, pinned with --require-hashes; fetches by URL+SHA-256 and writes deterministic output).
- `tools/checks/` (repo hygiene scripts), `schemas/` (JSON Schema 2020-12 for editors and the Python output check), `docs/adr/`, `docs/systems/<system>.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.github/workflows/{ci-linux.yml,ios.yml,nightly.yml}`, `.github/pull_request_template.md`.
Never commit archives. CI fails on *.zip, *.ipa or *.7z.

2) Dependency directions, enforced by the build and by a script that checks import lines per target. Core depends on nothing. Content depends on Core. Engine depends on Content and Core. AI and Presentation depend on Engine, Content and Core. simcli and App depend on all of those. MapRenderer depends only on Core, Content (the MapAsset reader) and a plain colour or overlay buffer handed over by App. Engine, AI and Presentation must never import UIKit, SwiftUI, Metal or Dispatch, and must never call Date(), Calendar, Timer, any .random API, or sin/cos/exp/log/pow (use Core.DMath). Platform services (file storage, compression, audio, haptics, thermal state) sit behind protocols implemented in App/Platform. The Engine stays 100% Linux-buildable, and that build is itself the proof.

3) Identity. Data files use lowercase namespaced string IDs matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_.]{1,47}$` (e.g. `sov`, `ddr`, `p.egy.cairo`, `tech.jet_engines_2`). IDs are never reused or renamed. Renames happen in loc files only, and real splits or merges go in `aliases.json`. At load the Interner maps each kind to dense Int32 indices sorted by ID, so file and pack order never matter. Use phantom-typed `Idx<Province>`, `Idx<Country>` and so on, so kinds cannot be mixed. Dynamic entities (armies, fleets, projects, treaties, later trade routes, companies and spies) use `Handle{index:Int32, generation:UInt32}` with free lists. Indices exist only at runtime: saves, commands logged to disk, and content never contain them.

4) Data model. `ContentDB` is an immutable final class shared by reference (province area, terrain, neighbours, coastal flag, sea-zone links, label anchors, unit types, techs, modifiers, defines). `WorldState` is a value-type struct of SoA tables (`ProvinceTable{owner:[Idx<Country>], controller, population:[Int64], ...}`, `CountryTable{treasury:[Int64], ...}`), a dense 200×200 country-pair table for relations, and handle tables. Snapshots use copy-on-write and cost O(1). Adding an entity kind means a new table, a system file, Command cases, a save section that defaults to empty for old saves, and a doc page, with no change to existing tables. Province geometry is versioned (`world-v1`). Each scenario declares the map version it needs. Province cuts must be the common refinement of every planned scenario's borders, and later splits are handled by alias migrations.

5) Content format and validation. Packs are folders of UTF-8 JSON with `pack.json` {id, version, formatVersion, dependsOn, mapVersion}. The base game is itself a pack, and scenario_1985 is another. One Swift validator, shared with runtime loading, runs in CI as `simcli validate content/`. It:
- rejects unknown keys through a strict decoder that compares keys against CodingKeys, because JSONDecoder silently ignores extras
- resolves every reference
- checks ranges and units
- checks that every province has exactly one owner per scenario
- checks adjacency symmetry
- checks that every `ar` loc key exists (English missing is a warning)
- checks that each ID matches its regex
- rejects duplicate IDs unless the later pack uses an explicit `override` block
- reports every error with file plus JSON pointer
Tuning numbers live only in `defines.json`. Bonuses live only in `modifiers.json`, a typed catalog with scope, stacking and clamp. Tech, laws, buildings, events, difficulty, presets (historical, strong, superpower, god) and cheats all apply modifiers instead of adding special cases in code. Events use a typed effect and condition vocabulary (Swift enums plus schema); there is no embedded scripting language in v1.

6) Simulation pipeline. One file `Engine/Pipeline.swift` owns the stage order and cadence. Every day:
- apply queued Commands, sorted by (tick, issuer, sequence)
- diplomacy expiry
- military movement, combat and occupation
- project and construction progress
- staggered AI: country i thinks when (day+i) % aiPeriod == 0
Every month:
- economy, through the ledger
- population
- stability and unrest
- research
- event checks (staggered)
- history sampling
Yearly: elections and other future systems.
Each system is `struct X: SimSystem { static let reads/writes: [Column]; func run(_: inout TickContext) }`. A test asserts that systems in the same phase never write the same column, which keeps a future parallel pre-step safe. Treasury changes only through `Ledger.post(country, category, amount)`. Notifications go into a bounded ring buffer (about 500), and pending player decisions have an expiry plus a default option, so the simulation never blocks. The simulation runs off the main thread. It publishes a COW snapshot to @MainActor at 10 Hz or less, and the UI only reads snapshots and submits Commands.

7) Commands and undo. Player UI, AI, cheats, rename-leader and cancel-project-with-partial-refund are all `enum Command: Codable, Sendable` with validate and apply. The AI cannot do anything the player cannot. While paused, issued commands sit in a visible 'pending orders' list that can be cancelled before time resumes; this is the undo for UI mistakes. There is no general state rollback. Each save keeps the command log since the last autosave. A 'report bug' share-sheet export bundles the autosave, command log, seed and content hash, and `simcli replay` reproduces it headless on Linux. Every fixed bug becomes a golden replay test.

8) Determinism kit in Core, all golden-value tested:
- DetRNG: SplitMix64 with counter-based derivation per (seed, day, stream, entity) and its own uniform-int and uniform-double mapping.
- DMath: deterministic exp, log, pow and smoothstep built only from + − × ÷ sqrt.
- Money and stocks as Int64 (money unit: constant 1985 USD, smallest unit $1k).
- GameDate: Int32 days since 1 Jan 1985 with its own Gregorian conversion.
- StateHasher (FNV-1a or xxHash64 over all columns).
CI runs the 1985 scenario for 2 years twice on x86_64 and on arm64 and requires identical hashes. Save, then load, then continue must match an uninterrupted run.

9) Saves. File `<slot>.sanei` holds:
- magic `SANEI`, a container version, a flags byte for compression
- metadata JSON {formatVersion, gameVersion, build, scenarioId, mapVersion, contentHash, packs, date, playerCountry, playtime, cheatsUsed, seed}
- a compressed payload: columnar JSON with a per-kind string ID list, where cross-references are indices into the save's own ID lists and are remapped on load
- a CRC32 or SHA-256 checksum
The Engine codec writes uncompressed bytes, so it is Linux-testable. Compression (LZFSE or zlib) lives in App/Platform. Migrations are `[Int: (inout JSONValue) throws -> Void]` steps applied v1→vN on the untyped tree, so old Swift structs are never kept. Content aliases remap renamed or split IDs, and new IDs missing from a save get scenario defaults. Golden saves in `Tests/Golden/saves/` are added at every formatVersion bump and every release, and never edited or deleted. CI loads each one, runs 30 days and checks invariants. Autosaves are monthly plus on app background (with a background task), rotate 3 slots, are written atomically (temp file plus rename) and are read back to verify. Saves live in Application Support/Saves, and an export button shares them.

10) Lightness budgets, written in docs/perf.md and enforced where possible:
- Daily tick: 1 ms mean and 4 ms p99 or less on a Linux CI runner (stored baseline; fail on more than 25% regression); monthly tick 10 ms or less. On device the target is 2 ms or less on the oldest supported iPhone, measured with os_signpost.
- Launch to menu 1.5 s or less, scenario load 2 s or less: memory-map `map.bin`, keep JSON content to about 3 MB or less, never parse GeoJSON on the device.
- Resident memory about 200 MB or less; IPA size gate (for example 5–80 MB).
- Renderer:
  - offline-triangulated meshes with 2–3 LODs and a per-vertex province index
  - map mode = rewrite the N×RGBA8 province colour buffer
  - each border segment stores its two province indices, so country borders follow ownership in the shader without CPU recomputation
  - MTKView paused plus enableSetNeedsDisplay, with frames driven only during gestures, inertia or visible changes
  - labels shaped once with Core Text, cached as textures, drawn at precomputed anchors
  - flags as one atlas, with a hi-res flag loaded lazily for the selected country
- HUD throttled to about 4 Hz with @Observable.
- Thermal state serious or Low Power Mode: cap at 30 fps and limit max speed. Critical: auto-reduce speed and show a toast.

11) Localization. UI strings go in `Localizable.xcstrings` with semantic keys (hud.treasury). Content strings go in `content/packs/*/loc/{ar,en}/*.json` with keys like country.sov.name, province.p.egy.cairo.name, event.<id>.title/desc/option.<n>. Both support the six CLDR Arabic plural forms. The Engine emits typed notifications (kind, IDs, numbers) and never text. Presentation's GameFormatter is the only place that formats numbers, money (compact scale words thousand, million, billion, trillion with 1985 USD), percentages and dates (Arabic month names from loc; choose one month-name convention in an ADR). It takes the digit setting through the `@numbers=arab|latn` locale subtag. The UI uses leading and trailing only. The map view is forced `.leftToRight`. Mixed Arabic and Latin runs use Unicode isolates. Use the system Arabic font, or only OFL-licensed fonts if custom. Seed province names from Natural Earth `name_ar` (4,589 of 4,596 filled), then review them by hand.

13) CI workflows. ci-linux.yml runs on every push and PR, as a matrix of ubuntu-24.04 and ubuntu-24.04-arm: swift build with warnings as errors, swift test, simcli validate, SwiftLint, the banned-API and imports script, jscpd new-clones gate, file-length gate, no-archives gate, generated-files hash check, and the cross-arch hash comparison. ios.yml runs on macos-26 with Xcode 26.x pinned (needed for App Store uploads since 2026-04-28) for PRs that touch App/ and for main and tags. It runs XcodeGen pinned by version and checksum, simulator tests, an unsigned archive with CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO, packages Payload into an IPA, and runs the IPA gate. The artifact is named `SaneiAlTarikh-<version>-<run>-<sha7>.ipa`, and a tag creates a GitHub Release. nightly.yml runs balance and performance trends. Turn on branch protection for main (required checks), which the user can do in GitHub web.

14) AI-assistant process. CLAUDE.md (≤150 lines) contains:
- a module map and dependency rules, the banned API list, and the one-command check `tools/checks/all.sh`
- 'search before you add': grep for an existing type or function, and extend or replace it in place, deleting the old code in the same PR
- no files or functions named *new, *v2, *fix, *patch, *old, and no commented-out code
- one primary type per file, named after it; files ≤400 lines (warning) and ≤600 (error); functions ≤60 lines
- every rule change updates docs/systems/<x>.md
- every new content field needs schema, validator, loc and a save default
- every save-format change bumps formatVersion and adds a migration plus a golden save
- every bug fix adds a replay or test
- PRs stay small (about 400 changed lines or fewer, excluding data)
ADRs follow Nygard (Context, Decision, Status, Consequences) and are immutable, superseded only by new ADRs. Definition of done: both CI workflows green, tests added, invariants pass, no new clones, docs and ADR updated, Arabic loc present, performance not regressed, licenses recorded for any new asset or data. The PR template carries the review checklist (dependency direction, duplication, determinism rules, mutation only through Commands or systems, constants in defines, save impact, performance impact, license). The AI works on a branch and opens a PR; the user reads the summary on the phone, merges, downloads the IPA and signs it. The user never uploads code by hand.

16) Feature growth path, with the base decision that makes each one additive:
- More scenarios: scenario = pack, start date and state as data, stable province IDs, versioned map with alias migrations.
- Naval and air warfare: the map pipeline emits sea zones, ports and coastal links in M1. Movement is a generic domain-filtered graph, and unit types carry a domain field.
- Trade: the economy already uses a goods vector and a categorised ledger; trade routes are a new handle table plus a stage between production and budget.
- Espionage: all UI reads of foreign data go through `Visibility.view(of:by:)`, which returns full data in M1. Spy actions become new Command cases and country-pair columns.

- Mods: base game is a pack, the same validator runs everywhere, overrides are explicit, and the content hash is stored in saves.
- English: no strings in the Engine, key-based catalogs, leading/trailing layout, a locale-driven formatter.
- iPad: adaptive SwiftUI layouts with no fixed pixel sizes and a resolution-independent renderer; enabling it is a project.yml device-family change plus a layout pass.
- More provinces: Int32 indices, LOD map.bin, colour-buffer map modes.
- Multiplayer (optional): Commands plus determinism already allow lockstep.
- Companies and corporations: a new handle table and system.
- iCloud saves: a single-file save container behind the Platform storage protocol.
- Sound and music: an AudioService protocol with cues keyed from notifications.

risks: The province set is built from present-day admin-1 units, which are not 1985 administrative units. Many countries reorganised regions after 1985. Realism here means correct 1985 national borders (USSR republics, GDR/FRG, North and South Yemen, Ethiopia with Eritrea, South-African-administered Namibia, Yugoslavia, Czechoslovakia, Sudan undivided, and so on) made from unions of modern units. This must be stated in an ADR so nobody later treats it as a bug.

Disputed and occupied territories in 1985 (Kashmir, Western Sahara, the West Bank, Gaza, Golan, northern Cyprus, Taiwan, the Falklands claim, and others) are politically sensitive for an Arabic-language commercial app. A data model that separates owner, controller and claims is needed from day one, along with an explicit display policy.

Cross-architecture floating-point determinism is not guaranteed if the compiler contracts multiply-add into FMA or a dependency uses libm. The x86_64-vs-arm64 hash test is the detector. The fallback is fixed-point arithmetic for rates.

Licensing: Natural Earth admin-1 attribute columns partly depend on GADM, which is non-commercial, per Natural Earth's own forum. Only geometry and names should be taken, and a lawyer should review before selling. CShapes and GADM must not feed any shipped geometry. Flags for 1985-era states must be sourced individually as public domain.
Over-engineering: a generic ECS framework or scripting language added too early would slow every milestone. Keep plain SoA tables, systems and typed enums, and add abstractions only through an ADR.

AI assistant drift: large PRs, re-implementing helpers that already exist, and skipping docs and tests. This is mitigated only if CI gates block merges, so branch protection must actually be turned on.
Toolchain drift: XcodeGen, Xcode and runner images change. Pin versions and checksums. GitHub deprecates macOS images (macOS 14 is already deprecated), so plan a yearly runner bump ADR.

Save performance: columnar JSON plus compression for about 5k provinces plus entities should be acceptable, but it is unmeasured on device. If encoding exceeds about 300 ms, a binary codec can replace it behind the same SaveCodec interface, with the same migration semantics.
The balance sanity bands are judgement calls. Bands set too tight will make nightly runs flaky, and bands set too loose will hide unrealistic outcomes. Start loose and tighten as systems mature.
On-device budgets (A12-class iPhone, thermal behaviour) cannot be tested in CI. Performance there depends on the user measuring on their own phone with the debug overlay and docs/perf.md.
